extraction_limitations: Atoms prioritize the study design, treatment exposure, endpoint definitions, major clinical outcomes, important intermediate/safety outcomes, prespecified subgroup findings, correction, conclusions, limitations, funding, and conflicts rather than atomizing every background citation or every individual cell in Tables 1-6.
No external sources were used to add study details not present in the primary PDF or correction.

The primary PDF itself contains the January 2003 Table 6 correction as appended material on PDF page 18; the separately supplied correction PDF was treated as the authoritative supporting correction and used to supersede original Table 6 values.

atoms.canonical_statement: ALLHAT tested whether first-step amlodipine or lisinopril reduced fatal coronary heart disease or nonfatal myocardial infarction and other cardiovascular outcomes compared with chlorthalidone in high-risk hypertension.
Participants were men and women aged 55 years or older with stage 1 or stage 2 hypertension and at least one additional coronary heart disease risk factor.

population.label: ALLHAT participants aged 55 years or older with hypertension and at least one additional coronary heart disease risk factor
inclusion_criteria: At least one additional CHD risk factor

atoms.canonical_statement: Individuals with a history of hospitalized or treated symptomatic heart failure or known left ventricular ejection fraction below 35% were excluded.

population.label: Potential ALLHAT participants
exclusion_criteria: History of hospitalized or treated symptomatic heart failure

atoms.canonical_statement: The analyzed antihypertensive comparison included 33,357 participants recruited at 623 centers in the United States, Canada, Puerto Rico, and the US Virgin Islands.

population.label: ALLHAT participants aged 55 years or older with hypertension and at least one additional coronary heart disease risk factor

atoms.canonical_statement: At baseline, mean age was 67 years; 47% of participants were women, 35% were Black, and 36% had diabetes, with nearly identical distributions across treatment groups.

population.label: ALLHAT participants aged 55 years or older with hypertension and at least one additional coronary heart disease risk factor

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants were randomly assigned by telephone to chlorthalidone, amlodipine, or lisinopril in a 1.7:1:1 ratio using a concealed computer-generated scheme stratified by center with random block sizes of 5 or 9.
Chlorthalidone was assigned as first-step therapy at 12.5 mg/day with a sham titration step and a maximum dose of 25 mg/day.

exposures.details: initial dose; sham titration at 12.5 mg; maximum 25 mg/day

atoms.canonical_statement: Amlodipine was assigned as first-step therapy at 2.5 mg/day and could be titrated to 5 mg/day and then 10 mg/day.
Lisinopril was assigned as first-step therapy at 10 mg/day and could be titrated to 20 mg/day and then 40 mg/day.
The blood-pressure goal was below 140/90 mm Hg; when needed, open-label step 2 atenolol, clonidine, or reserpine and step 3 hydralazine were added.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary outcome was the composite of fatal coronary heart disease or nonfatal myocardial infarction.

outcome.definition: Composite of fatal coronary heart disease or nonfatal myocardial infarction

atoms.canonical_statement: All-cause mortality was a prespecified major secondary outcome.
Fatal or nonfatal stroke was a prespecified major secondary outcome.

outcome.definition: Fatal or nonfatal stroke

atoms.canonical_statement: Combined coronary heart disease included the primary outcome, coronary revascularization, and hospitalized angina.

outcome.definition: Fatal CHD or nonfatal MI, coronary revascularization, and hospitalized angina

atoms.canonical_statement: Combined cardiovascular disease included combined CHD, stroke, treated angina, heart failure, and peripheral arterial disease.

outcome.definition: Combined CHD, stroke, treated angina, fatal/hospitalized/treated nonhospitalized heart failure, and peripheral arterial disease

atoms.canonical_statement: Two prespecified major safety outcomes were hospitalization for gastrointestinal bleeding and angioedema.

outcome.definition: Hospitalization for gastrointestinal bleeding and angioedema

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary analyses were intention-to-treat; cumulative event rates used Kaplan-Meier methods and relative risks with 95% confidence intervals were estimated primarily with Cox proportional hazards models.
ALLHAT had 83% power to detect a 16% reduction in the primary outcome for each active comparison with chlorthalidone at a two-sided alpha of .0178.
Mean follow-up was 4.9 years and 99% of expected person-years were observed in all three treatment groups.
At 5 years, 80.5% of chlorthalidone participants, 80.4% of amlodipine participants, and 72.6% of lisinopril participants were taking the assigned study drug or another drug in the same class.

atoms.canonical_statement: The correction states that the replacement data for Table 6 do not affect the results or conclusions of the original ALLHAT article.
A later correction appended to the primary PDF states that Pasquale F. Nestico, MD, was inadvertently omitted from the ALLHAT investigator list and should appear under Pennsylvania on page 2996.

The authors concluded that thiazide-type diuretics should be considered first for pharmacologic therapy in patients with hypertension because they were unsurpassed in lowering blood pressure and reducing clinical events and were less costly.
Because many participants required more than one drug for blood-pressure control, the authors inferred that a diuretic should be included in multidrug regimens when possible.
ALLHAT did not evaluate newer antihypertensive agents such as angiotensin-receptor blockers and selective aldosterone antagonists that became available after the trial was designed.
Equivalent blood-pressure reduction was not fully achieved across randomized groups; mean follow-up systolic pressure was higher with lisinopril than chlorthalidone, especially in Black participants.

The permitted step-up regimen produced a somewhat artificial treatment sequence, including greater reliance on sympatholytic drugs rather than diuretics or calcium channel blockers in the ACE-inhibitor group.

Direct randomized evidence in this report applies to chlorthalidone, amlodipine, and lisinopril; broader application to their drug classes was an inference made by the authors using other trial evidence.
